title: podman run --rm can deadlock with its own `container cleanup`, permanently wedging the per-UID SHM lock
body:
### Issue Description

A rootless `podman run --rm` deadlocked with the `podman container cleanup`
process that conmon spawns on container exit. The parent `run` holds the
container's SHM semaphore and waits for its child to finish; the cleanup child
waits for that same semaphore. Neither ever exits.

Because `/dev/shm/libpod_rootless_lock_<uid>` is shared by every rootless podman
invocation of that UID — across all `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` storages — the
wedged semaphore is not contained to the affected container. Every later podman
command that needs any container lock then blocks forever, including commands
that are not about containers at all (`podman ps -a`, `podman info`, and
`podman inspect NAME` when NAME does not exist).

One deadlocked container blocked an automated build pipeline for six weeks.
Every new run added another permanently hung podman process; 13 had accumulated
by the time it was diagnosed. Meanwhile `podman version`, `podman images`,
`podman network ls` and `podman image exists` kept working normally, which made
the failure look like a storage problem rather than a lock problem.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Not reproducible on demand — it is a race in the cleanup path. It happened once
under sustained load: a few hundred `podman run --rm` invocations per day over
roughly six weeks, several concurrent at a time, sharing one UID across several
`CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` storages.

1. Run `podman run --rm <image> <command>` repeatedly and concurrently as a
   rootless user.
2. Occasionally one invocation never exits: the container has finished, conmon
   sits in `do_wait`, and the `podman container cleanup --stopped-only --rm <cid>`
   child is blocked on a futex.
3. From then on, every podman command of that UID that touches container locks
   hangs indefinitely, in any storage, until the stuck process is killed.

### Describe the results you received

Process tree at capture, elapsed 1 day 12 h. The shell that started the run had
already been SIGKILLed by an external supervisor, so the top of the chain is
reparented to init while the podman processes stayed alive:

    PID      PPID     WCHAN             CMD
    3514586  1        -                 <login shell>
    3514705  3514586  -                 <wrapper script>
    3530915  3514705  -                 <wrapper script>
    3531787  3530915  -                 <wrapper script>
    3568436  3531787  futex_wait_queue  podman run --rm -v <dir>:<dir> <image> sh -c "<command>"
    3569532  1        do_wait           conmon --api-version 1 -c <cid> -r /usr/bin/runc ... --exit-command podman ... container cleanup --stopped-only --rm <cid>
    3574622  3569532  futex_wait_queue  podman ... container cleanup --stopped-only --rm <cid>

The SHM segment shows semaphore 4 held by a **live** owner. The bitmap at
offset 0x38 is 0x11 (semaphores 0 and 4 allocated); `locks[n]` sits at
`0x40 + 40n`, so `locks[4]` is at offset 0xe0:

    $ dd if=/dev/shm/libpod_rootless_lock_1001 bs=1 skip=224 count=4 | od -An -tu4
    lock word        = 0x8036733d
    owner TID        = 3568445   -> /proc/3568436/task/3568445 (the parent `podman run`)
    FUTEX_WAITERS    = 1
    FUTEX_OWNER_DIED = 0

Every mutex in the segment has `__kind = 0x290`, so `PTHREAD_MUTEX_ROBUST` is
set — but robust recovery never fires, because the owner is alive, merely
blocked.

The three processes wait on different things, which closes the cycle. Comparing
each process's futex addresses against its own mapping of the SHM segment:

    PID 3574622 (container cleanup)
      mapping   7a6c083f8000-7a6c0840d000  /dev/shm/libpod_rootless_lock_1001
      futex     0x7a6c083f80e0             -> offset 0xe0 == locks[4]
      => waiting for semaphore 4

    PID 3568436 (podman run --rm, the recorded owner of semaphore 4)
      mapping   7f2326e12000-7f2326e27000  /dev/shm/libpod_rootless_lock_1001
      futexes   0xc000... and 0x2ed.../0x2ef...   (Go heap and runtime only)
      => NOT waiting on the segment: it holds semaphore 4 and is blocked in the
         Go runtime, waiting for its child to finish

    PID 3569532 (conmon)
      no futex; WCHAN = do_wait
      => waiting for the cleanup child it spawned

So: `podman run --rm` holds semaphore 4 and waits for conmon's child; conmon
waits for `container cleanup`; `container cleanup` waits for semaphore 4.

An unrelated, freshly started podman confirms where waiters pile up
(`GOTRACEBACK=all`, then `SIGQUIT`):

    runtime.cgocall
    libpod/lock/shm._Cfunc_lock_semaphore(0x..., 0x4)
    libpod/lock/shm.(*SHMLocks).LockSemaphore(0x..., 0x4)
            libpod/lock/shm/shm_lock.go:227
    libpod/lock.(*SHMLock).Lock(...)
            libpod/lock/shm_lock_manager_linux.go:127
    libpod.(*Container).GetNetworkStatus(...)
            libpod/container.go:1486
    pkg/domain/infra/abi.(*ContainerEngine).GetContainerNetStatuses(...)
            pkg/domain/infra/abi/network.go:292
    pkg/domain/infra/abi.(*ContainerEngine).NetworkInspect(...)
            pkg/domain/infra/abi/network.go:72
    cmd/podman/inspect.(*inspector).inspect(...)
            cmd/podman/inspect/inspect.go:137
    cmd/podman/inspect.Inspect(...)
            cmd/podman/inspect/inspect.go:46

Measured behaviour of a fresh podman while that one container lock is wedged
(15 s timeout; rc=124 means it hung, rc=125 means "no such object"):

    podman version                          rc=0
    podman images                           rc=0
    podman network ls                       rc=0
    podman image exists MISSING             rc=1
    podman inspect --type image MISSING     rc=125
    podman inspect --type container MISSING rc=125
    podman inspect --type pod MISSING       rc=125
    podman inspect --type volume MISSING    rc=125
    podman inspect --type network MISSING   rc=124   <-- hangs
    podman inspect MISSING (no --type)      rc=124   <-- hangs
    podman ps -a                            rc=124   <-- hangs
    podman info                             rc=124   <-- hangs

`podman info` produces no output and no error message at all — it simply never
returns. Note that this is the one command this bug report form requires, so
while the lock is wedged the required diagnostics cannot be collected.

Killing the lock owner (`kill -9` on the `podman run --rm` process alone) was
enough to resolve everything, and the recovery path behaved exactly as it
should:

    $ kill -9 3568436 ; sleep 5
    lock word        = 0x00000000
    owner TID        = 0
    FUTEX_OWNER_DIED = 0
    $ ps -p 3569532,3574622    # conmon and container cleanup
    (both gone)

The kernel set `FUTEX_OWNER_DIED` on semaphore 4, the waiting `container
cleanup` woke with `EOWNERDEAD`, marked the mutex consistent, finished removing
the container and exited on its own; conmon followed. All queued commands
drained, and `podman info` then reported `freeLocks: 2047`.

In other words the robust-mutex machinery works correctly — nothing is
corrupted, and no `podman system renumber` was needed. The bug is purely the
wait cycle between `run --rm`, conmon and `container cleanup`: as long as all
three stay alive, nothing can break it.

### Describe the results you expected

1. `podman run --rm` and the `container cleanup` process it spawns should not be
   able to deadlock on the same container lock.

2. A container stuck in that state should not be able to block unrelated podman
   invocations of the same UID indefinitely. A bounded wait, or an option in the
   spirit of `--lock-timeout`, would turn a permanent outage into a command that
   fails with a clear message. As it stands there is no diagnostic at all: the
   command simply never returns and never prints anything.

### podman info output

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

Rootless podman built from upstream source (not distribution-packaged),
v5.8.0, commit 07efc23e05c3d9aa15a0f30d57194737bfc4b6b1, Go 1.24.2.
Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-124-generic, x86_64, bare metal.

Storage driver `overlay` on xfs with `Native Overlay Diff: false` (fuse-overlayfs
mount program), runtime runc 1.3.3, DB backend sqlite, network backend
netavark 1.11.0, cgroup manager systemd, conmon 2.1.12, buildah 1.43.0.

Several independent `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` files are used by the same UID for
different workloads. Note that this does *not* isolate them: the SHM lock
segment is per-UID, so a container wedged in one storage blocks podman in all of
them.


### Additional information

Happens only occasionally — once in roughly six weeks of continuous load. The
host had not been rebooted since before the incident (uptime 78 days) and
lingering is enabled for the user in question, so the runtime directory was
never recreated underneath the running processes.

The supervisor that drives these runs kills a job's shell with SIGKILL on
timeout, which leaves the podman process tree orphaned but alive. That is how
the deadlocked processes survived for six weeks unnoticed.

What made this hard to diagnose is that the failure is completely silent. No
error, no log line, no timeout — affected commands just never return, and the
commands that do work (`version`, `images`, `network ls`, `image exists`) make
the storage look perfectly healthy.

comments.body:
If this happens again please send SIGABRT to to both podman processes simultaneously and capture the stderr of the process if possible. Or alternativly attach with the delve go debugger and get the goroutine trace that way. The cleanup command may run in the background without stderr/out so that is likely required for that.

Also please see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/community/blob/main/LLM_POLICY.md, I assume the output here is AI generated, it certainly is quite verbose with unnecessary details. Other commands hanging are not relevant here if there is a deadlock race between run/cleanup commands.

I See the inspect issue was reported as https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29647 which is fine so no need to have all these details here.

In general we only support the latest upstream release so it would be good if you can use podman 6.1 and test with that. Or at least provide a scripted reproducer somehow to trigger the race. Without a solid reproducer we can just guess.
